materials.text:
# file-lifecycle-hygiene：Gate heavy-test cost evidence

Created 2026-10-14 (Asia/Shanghai); baseline HEAD `0fe55d31ecb11eadf4999b534a0767d08d68bd90`.
Purpose: current-version baseline, isolated attribution and same-workload remeasurement for package-tools/Core closure and Product supporting Check tests.
Status: task-owned ignored auxiliary evidence. Keep raw before/after logs, source manifests and measurement scripts until this optimization is audited; no automatic deletion or commit.
Measurements are sequential, Bun 1.3.14 through mise, existing caches retained, unchanged timeout/concurrency/quality limits. Child CPU is waited descendant accounting; RSS is the maximum single-child high-water mark, not total process-tree memory. Profiles are separate from timing samples.

## Workloads and source identity

`supporting-lane-files.txt` is the exact 19-file set returned by the current public Gate lane resolver. Original source-only baseline and final manifests cover tracked src/scripts plus package/toolchain root inputs; their digests are respectively `baaba93b27a3ee9c23064b1c9a5502abb0273d3805005bd19f8fab2736dec0e7` and `c1a296e367ef9ff71739a21090e4e2f1698a5fc6156c36c8c14dceee5c71ec69`. Only the two owned scripts/validation TS files differ; Product and validator implementations are unchanged.

`measure-command.py` captures stdout/stderr and child resources in exclusive new labels. Core and supporting lanes each have a warmup and three baseline observations. Final formatted Core has a separate warmup and three final observations. Supporting sources are unchanged, so its after observations are controls, not an optimization result. No reliable p95 is inferred from three samples.

| Workload | Before median | Final/control median | Boundary |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Core test process wall | 5043.50 ms | 1324.83 ms | Final formatted source; original 19-row matrix retained, additional actual no-emit type-error assertion. |
| Core child-tree CPU | 10157.57 ms | 2002.26 ms | Waited descendant accounting, not Gate CPU or aggregate memory. |
| Supporting lane wall | 5312.08 ms | 5110.88 ms | No source change; difference is not attributed to this patch. |
| Non-interleaved complete Gate wall | 41667.05 ms | 49895.82 ms | All 6 invocations 43/43; large variation, docs/Case changed, not an isolated or positive Gate speedup result. |

`core-attribution-before.jsonl` records delegated TypeScript sys.readFile observation on valid fixtures: boundary reads 129 files, including 68 Node type files, versus 18 / 0 with explicit minimal environment. Single boundary/no-emit timings were 374.77/395.29 ms versus 18.66/68.12 ms; these are attribution observations, not repeated timing medians or CPU profiles.

## Interleaved complete Gate control

`paired-gate.py` alternated old fixture compiler environment and final explicit environment in A/B, B/A, A/B order. It kept the final test assertions (including TS2345 rejection), current docs/Case, Product, validator, candidate and Gate configuration fixed. The only temporary variant was the owned test-support file; exact source snapshots/hash are in `paired-*-fixture.source.txt` and `paired-source-identity.json`. Final source was restored and verified by the script's finally guard.

The old-environment variant is a control with final assertions, not an exact replay of initial HEAD. Each pair's wall change was -19.72%, -15.48%, +0.22%; two of three improved. Baseline/final group medians were 39088.59/34615.02 ms (an observed 11.44% median reduction). All six invocations passed 43/43 and used `0.0.0-local.dfb5e87283d2`. Existing caches and learned scheduling history were retained and used/updated normally, not frozen; these three pairs do not establish a causal or universal Gate speedup. No threshold, timeout, waiver, priority or concurrency change was used.

The primary adoption evidence is the bounded fixture's consistent local wall/CPU reduction, removal of irrelevant ambient declaration reads, and preserved/improved proof signal. Check mean/p95 warnings remain in complete Gate observations. Last paired final invocation: `/workspace/vibe-check/.log/project-gate/2026-10-14T06-26-03.165Z-2828243-2a0ee315-8107-4e42-abf9-3b365d738422/`.

## Validation and unsuccessful attempts

- scripts typecheck/lint, exact two-file Oxfmt, both target tests (2/2), public validate, full 722 entities / 181 Cases / 15 topics closure passed on final code. Independent non-implementation review found no blocking proof/style/docs issue.
- First pre-format after Gate was 42/43: only Source format failed. Oxfmt changed the assert.throws layout; final source received fresh Core and complete Gate samples, all passed. Failed log retained: `/workspace/vibe-check/.log/project-gate/2026-10-14T06-14-58.544Z-2789543-dcf4d521-7788-4686-a282-388cd35c9f51/`.
- Initial supporting warmup used unsupported `dev:test`; it exited before tests and is excluded. The replacement used actual files from the lane resolver.
- Bun test accepted the CPU profiling flags but emitted no profile file; `profile-core.*.log` is only another passing test observation, not CPU profile evidence.

## Reproduction and lifecycle

From the repository root, use `uv run --no-project python tmp/gate-heavy-tests-20261014/measure-command.py <unused-label> mise exec -- bun test scripts/validation/package-tools-core-closure.test.ts`, or the same wrapper with `bun run check -- --all`. Supporting uses the saved exact lane paths. `summarize-measurements.py` produces `measurement-summary.json`. Attribution uses `mise exec -- bun run tmp/gate-heavy-tests-20261014/core-attribution.ts` and is separate from timing.

The paired script uses exclusive labels and exact final source guards; its already populated destinations are not a retry target. Copy/adapt to a new task-owned evidence directory if repetition is needed. Keep original logs/manifests and both controlled source snapshots until review no longer needs replay; do not add them to current test discovery or treat them as stable rules. No Git add/commit/push or Change deletion was performed.
